name: The Wondrous Wisdomball: a summoned ball lists the dungeon's own quests and takes the ones a chain hides
contract: Spell 83050 summons creature 79025, the companion that carries the quests of the dungeon its owner is standing in and takes them back. The ball owns no quest relations of its own, so its marker, its quest list and its quest packets are the server's script answering for it. What this scenario proves: using item 101169 teaches the summon; the summon produces a creature the player owns; in a dungeon whose own spawns hand out quests, the ball reports an available marker (8) for that player; a quest whose chain is not finished is refused by the game's own rules yet still granted and handed in at the ball; the list holds the whole dungeon's quests, including ones no creature inside it hands out; a quest the character has taken moves out of the offered half and into the carried one; and out in the world the ball offers nothing, still lists the dungeon quests being carried, marks itself as their turn-in point, and hands one in there. It is one summon for everyone at it: a second player standing by somebody else's ball is listed their own carried quests, is marked the same hand-in point, and can open that window and hand their quest in there, while the summoner's log is left alone. Both clicks a name in that frame can produce are exercised as the client sends them - the query of an offered name, and the complete-quest of one already carried - and each is required to be answered by the ball's own script rather than dropped. The frame's greeting row is asserted by id. The gossip list as the client draws it, the window a click opens and the client's rendering of a right-click on a pet are outside this harness's reach.

steps.label: Let the dungeon map, its spawns and level scaling settle
A fresh character knows neither the summon nor has the item
The companion is obtained, as a purchase would obtain it
The Wisdomball item is in the bag
Using the item teaches its summon
The summon is now in the spellbook
Summon the ball
Let the summon land in the world
The cast produced a creature this player owns
In a dungeon the ball reports an available marker, so the client draws the ! over it
Record the bag contents before the hand-in
The chained quest is not in the log yet
The game itself refuses it, because its chain is unfinished - this is the gap the ball fills
Accept it at the ball anyway
The ball granted the quest the game refused, and it arrived ready to hand in
Finish its objectives, as a dungeon run would
Hand it in at the ball
The hand-in left the log and the quest is marked rewarded, so the ball paid it out
And the chosen reward is in the bag
The ball lists the whole dungeon, not just the NPCs standing inside it
A Blackrock Depths quest no creature inside it hands out is listed for it anyway
Click that offered name, as the client does in the frame's available half
The window it opens asks for the quest rather than taking it
The greeting the frame draws above the list is a row the server can send
Nothing is carried yet, so the list is the dungeon's own quests only
Take a second dungeon quest at the ball
It is in the log now, and the list shows it as one the character carries
And it is no longer counted as something still to be offered
Taken, it is unfinished: it asks for an item the character is not carrying
So the ball lists it as carried and not as ready to hand in
Carry back the item the quest asks for, as the dungeon would drop it
Click its name at the ball while it is still unfinished - carried, so this is the complete-quest opcode
The ball's window is what finishes it, as the quest giver's own window would
Now it counts as ready to hand in at the ball
Walk back out into the world
Let the map change land
Have the ball out in the world
Let the summon land
The ball is out here too
But it offers no dungeon's quests out here
It still lists the dungeon quest the character is carrying
And with something ready to hand in it marks itself out here too
Click the same carried name out here, where the ball has no dungeon of its own
Opening it left it where it was, ready to hand in and unhanded
Hand it in at the ball, out of the dungeon
The hand-in went through out here, so the ball is the turn-in point wherever it is summoned
With nothing carried the list is empty again
And the marker is gone with it
A second player walks up to the ball somebody else summoned
Let that teleport land
The second player carries a dungeon quest of their own
The ball lists it for them, though the ball is not theirs
And the summoner's own list stays their own
The ball marks itself for the other player as a hand-in point too
Clicking the carried name opens its window at another player's ball
The window left their quest where it was, ready and unhanded
Hand it in at the ball the other player summoned
The hand-in went through for them, so the summon serves everyone at it
The summoner's own copy of that quest was not touched by it
